+# Backlog
+
+**Staged from:** `.pm/PLAN_SUMMARY.md`, `documentation/PLAN.md`, `deep-research-report.md`
+
+---
+
+## Phase M1 — Research & Backend Selection (Weeks 1–2)
+
+| #  | Item                                                                                     | Notes                                                    |
+|----|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|
+| 1.1 | Set up Python environment with MMPose, RTMPose, RTMO                                     | Official install from OpenMMLab docs                     |
+| 1.2 | Benchmark RTMPose-m vs RTMO on target hardware (CPU/GPU)                                | RTMO not yet evaluated per PLAN_SUMMARY                    |
+| 1.3 | ONNX export validation for chosen model                                                    | Required for future optimization (Phase 5)                |
+
+## Phase M2 — External Tracking Runner (Weeks 1–2, overlap)
+
+| #  | Item                                                                                     | Notes                                                    |
+|----|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|
+| 2.1 | Build MMPose worker (standalone Python script, CLI entrypoint)                          | Out-of-process by design per PLAN_SUMMARY                  |
+| 2.2 | Implement video-to-JSON inference pipeline                                                | MMPose inferencer → cached JSON outputs                   |
+| 2.3 | Establish tracking result schema                                                           | Must encode 2D keypoints + track IDs per person           |
+
+## Phase M3 — Blender Add-on Skeleton (Weeks 2–3)
+
+| #  | Item                                                                                     | Notes                                                    |
+|----|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|
+| 3.1 | Create Blender add-on panel (video input, person selection, output mode)                 | Follows Blender developer conventions                      |
+| 3.2 | Implement subprocess launcher (Blender Python → MMPose worker)                           | JSON-first communication via cached files                 |
+| 3.3 | Implement JSON import from worker output                                                  | Frame-to-frame data exchange                              |
+
+## Phase M4 — Visualization in Blender (Week 3)
+
+| #  | Item                                                                                     | Notes                                                    |
+|----|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|
+| 4.1 | Map MMPose keypoints to Blender empties at joint positions                                | 17 COCO body joints per person                            |
+| 4.2 | Add track ID visualization in Blender viewport                                            | Persistent IDs across frames                              |
+| 4.3 | Implement basic temporal smoothing on empty positions between frames                      | Gap fill + interpolation                                  |
+
+## Phase M5 — Retargeting & Animation Mapping (Weeks 5–8)
+
+| #  | Item                                                                                     | Notes                                                    |
+|----|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|
+| 5.1 | Skeleton bone mapping (MMPose 17 joints → Blender armature)                              | Rigify, Humanoid, Mixamo presets                          |
+| 5.2 | Automatic armature generation from pose tracks                                            | Phase 2 deliverable                                       |
+| 5.3 | IK/FK retargeting options                                                                | User-selectable                                           |
+| 5.4 | Animation curve generation from pose keyframes                                            | Populated from tracked motion                             |
+| 5.5 | Gap-filling for occluded frames                                                          | Interpolation or ML fill (50+ frame occlusions)           |
+
+## Phase M6 — Multi-Person + Object Tracking (Weeks 9–12)
+
+| #  | Item                                                                                     | Notes                                                    |
+|----|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|
+| 6.1 | Integrate SAM 2 for promptable object masks                                                | Phase 3 deliverable                                       |
+| 6.2 | Integrate ByteTrack for general MOT                                                       | Non-human objects in crowded scenes                       |
+| 6.3 | SAM 2 + MMPose composite pipeline                                                         | SAM finds person → MMPose tracks pose                     |
+| 6.4 | Object mask overlays in Blender (compositing/roto)                                       |                                                         |
+
+## Phase M7 — UI Workflow (Weeks 3–8, iterative)
+
+| #  | Item                                                                                     | Notes                                                    |
+|----|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|
+| 7.1 | Retarget mode selector + bone mapping config UI                                           |                                                         |
+| 7.2 | Tooltips, presets, keyboard shortcuts                                                    | Phase 5 polish                                            |
+| 7.3 | User workflow testing on diverse rigs                                                      |                                                         |
+
+## Phase M8 — 3D Pose Lifting (Weeks 13–15, if licensing permits)
+
+| #  | Item                                                                                     | Notes                                                    |
+|----|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|
+| 8.1 | SMPL / WHAM licensing compliance check                                                    | Major blocker                                             |
+| 8.2 | Optional 2D→3D pose lift from MMPose keypoints                                            | WHAM or alternative                                       |
+| 8.3 | Camera-relative → world-space transform                                                   |                                                         |
+| 8.4 | Fallback to 2D-only when 3D fails                                                         |                                                         |
+
+## Phase M9 — Optimization & Polish (Weeks 16–18)
+
+| #  | Item                                                                                     | Notes                                                    |
+|----|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|
+| 9.1 | End-to-end profiling (Blender → MMPose → Blender)                                        |                                                         |
+| 9.2 | ONNX export of RTMPose                                                                    | Faster inference                                          |
+| 9.3 | TensorRT backend for GPU optimization                                                     |                                                         |
+| 9.4 | Testing 50+ diverse video sequences                                                       |                                                         |
+| 9.5 | Documentation, tutorials, demo reel                                                       |                                                         |
+
+---
+
+## Dependencies & Blockers
+
+- Phase M6 (SAM 2, ByteTrack) depends on Phase M5 stabilizing first.
+- Phase M8 (3D lifting) is blocked until SMPL licensing is resolved.
+- Hardware requirements are undefined — no target GPU/CPU specification in source plans.
+- Blender version target is unspecified — add-on API compatibility is an open decision.

+# Architecture Decision Log
+
+**Source-plan context:** `.pm/PLAN_SUMMARY.md`, `documentation/PLAN.md`, `deep-research-report.md`
+
+---
+
+## ADR-1: Out-of-Process Inference
+
+**Decision:** All ML inference (MMPose, SAM 2, ByteTrack, WHAM) runs as separate Python subprocesses outside Blender's embedded Python.
+
+**Rationale:** Blender ships its own Python distribution. Embedding PyTorch/CUDA inside Blender's environment is complex and fragile. A separate process avoids DLL conflicts, simplifies dependency management, and lets Blender remain stable even if the inference worker crashes.
+
+**Consequences:**
+- Communication must use IPC (cached JSON files are the default).
+- The MMPose worker requires its own Python environment with PyTorch installed.
+- Slightly higher latency for large data transfer, justified by the decoupling benefit.
+
+**Status:** **Accepted** — mandated by all three planning sources.
+
+---
+
+## ADR-2: JSON-First Communication
+
+**Decision:** Data exchange between the MMPose worker and Blender uses cached JSON files, not in-memory pipes or shared libraries.
+
+**Rationale:** JSON files provide a durable, inspectable, and debuggable exchange format. They decouple the inference pipeline from the Blender UI thread. This enables offline processing and re-running steps without re-tracking raw video.
+
+**Consequences:**
+- Requires a defined tracking result schema (BACKLOG item 2.3).
+- File I/O becomes a performance factor — profiled in Phase 9.
+- Parallel workers require unique file paths or lock mechanisms.
+
+**Status:** **Accepted** — mandated by all three planning sources.
+
+---
+
+## ADR-3: MMPose/RTMPose as Primary Backend
+
+**Decision:** MMPose (RTMPose family) is the primary pose estimation backend. SAM 2 and ByteTrack are phase-two additions. LoRATv2 is deprecated for v1.
+
+**Rationale:** LoRATv2 outputs bounding boxes, not pose keypoints. Blender users need skeleton tracking for animation, camera rigging, and retargeting. MMPose provides 17 standard COCO keypoints per person with real-time performance (90+ FPS CPU, 430+ FPS GPU).
+
+**Consequences:**
+- Only 17 body joints are tracked in v1 — spine/neck/jaw/finger bones are interpolated.
+- SAM 2/ByteTrack integration is deferred to phase M6.
+- LoRATv2 may be retained as a camera-solving fallback (bounding boxes for tracking reference).
+
+**Status:** **Accepted** — resolution documented in PLAN_SUMMARY contradiction section.
+
+---
+
+## ADR-4: Empties as v1 Output
+
+**Decision:** Phase 1 output is Blender empties at keypoint positions. Armature retargeting is deferred to phase M5.
+
+**Rationale:** The source plan explicitly lists armature retargeting as Phase 2 (weeks 5–8). Starting with empties provides immediate value (motion paths, visualization) without the complexity of skeleton mapping.
+
+**Consequences:**
+- Users get pose tracks → empties with motion paths in v1.
+- Full animation pipeline requires Phase 2 delivery.
+- The choice of empty vs. armature for v1 is intentional ambiguity (see Unresolved Decisions below).
+
+**Status:** **Accepted** — aligns with phased plan in documentation/PLAN.md.
+
+---
+
+## Unresolved Decisions
+
+### RTMPose-m vs. RTMO for v1
+RTMPose-m has higher COCO AP (75.8); RTMO is faster for multi-person. The source plans do not resolve this. Recommendation: try both during M1 benchmarking (backlog item 1.2).
+
+### Blender version target
+No Blender version is specified in any source plan. Add-on API compatibility (e.g., `bpy.types.Panel` changes between 3.x and 4.x) is a decision that must be made.
+
+### Hardware requirements
+No GPU/CPU requirements are defined. GPU inference needs CUDA-capable hardware; CPU-only targets need RTMPose quantization strategy.
+
+### Distribution model
+Open-source marketplace add-on vs. paid release is undefined. No source plan addresses this.
+
+### SMPL licensing path
+WHAM requires SMPL/SMPLify registration. It is unclear whether a legal/compliance path exists. If blocked, WHAM should be replaced with an alternative (e.g., VideoPose3D).

+# Project Brief — Blender Motion Tracking Enhancement
+
+---
+
+## Purpose
+
+Integrate state-of-the-art human pose tracking into Blender's Video Editor for automatic camera rigging, motion retargeting, and animation. The system takes video input, produces 2D pose tracks with persistent IDs, maps them to Blender empties or armature bones, and optionally lifts to 3D.
+
+## Planning Sources
+
+The project scope is defined by three planning documents:
+
+- **`.pm/PLAN_SUMMARY.md`** — Technical planning summary derived from the master plan and deep research report.
+- **`documentation/PLAN.md`** — 18-week phased implementation plan with milestones and phases.
+- **`deep-research-report.md`** — Comparative analysis of candidate tracking backends (MMPose, SAM 2, ByteTrack, LoRATv2, WHAM).
+
+---
+
+## Recommended Architecture
+
+```
+Video / Still Images
+    → Blender Add-on Panel (launch MMPose worker, configure options)
+        → MMPose Worker (external Python subprocess, RTMPose inference)
+            → 2D Keypoints + Track IDs (cached JSON)
+                → Temporal Smoothing + Gap Fill
+                    → Blender Empties / Armature Bones
+                        → Optional 3D Pose Lift (WHAM, phase-dependent)
+                            → Animation Curves in Scene
+```
+
+## Primary Backend: MMPose / RTMPose
+
+MMPose with RTMPose is the recommended v1 backend. It produces 2D keypoints directly mappable to Blender bones and empties, with real-time performance (90+ FPS on CPU, 430+ FPS on GPU) and an Apache-2.0 license.
+
+## Target Phases
+
+1. **MMPose Integration** (Weeks 1–4): Video → MMPose → empties with keypoints + track IDs.
+2. **Armature Retargeting** (Weeks 5–8): Skeleton bone mapping, automatic armature generation, animation curves.
+3. **Multi-Person + Object Tracking** (Weeks 9–12): SAM 2, ByteTrack, RTMO integration.
+4. **3D Pose Lifting** (Weeks 13–15): Optional 2D→3D lift via WHAM.
+5. **Optimization & Polish** (Weeks 16–18): Latency optimization, TensorRT, UI polish, documentation.
+
+## Why Heavy ML Inference Runs Outside Blender (v1)
+
+Blender ships its own bundled Python distribution. Embedding PyTorch and CUDA inside Blender's Python environment introduces significant complexity:
+
+- **Dependency conflicts:** Blender's Python has its own version and bundled packages. Adding PyTorch (1200+ MB) and CUDA toolkits risks DLL conflicts.
+- **Stability:** A crash in the ML worker would take Blender down with it if embedded. Out-of-process keeps Blender stable.
+- **Distribution:** Shipping a combined Blender + PyTorch installer is impractical — PyTorch alone is 1.2+ GB with CUDA dependencies.
+- **Flexibility:** A separate worker lets users upgrade PyTorch independently, supports GPU/CPU toggle, and enables headless operation on a remote machine.
+
+The out-of-process design is mandated by all three planning sources.
+
+## Why Blender Consumes Cached Tracking Outputs
+
+Communication between Blender and the MMPose worker uses cached JSON files — not in-memory pipes or embedded libraries — because:
+
+- **Inspection & debugging:** JSON files are human-readable. Users can inspect tracking results, compare frames, and debug ID switches without rerunning inference.
+- **Idempotency:** Tracking outputs can be cached and reused. Users can tweak visualization, retargeting, or smoothing without re-tracking video.
+- **Decoupling:** The worker and Blender can run independently. The worker can process multiple videos; Blender can import any cached result at any time.
+- **Simplicity:** File-based exchange avoids complex IPC protocols, shared memory, or network sockets.
+
+## Key Constraints
+
+1. **Not a Python project** — deliverable is a Blender add-on, not a standalone Python repo.
+2. **Monocular 3D ambiguity** — 3D pose lifting is optional; depth recovery from a single camera is inherently ambiguous.
+3. **Identity consistency** — crowded scenes require robust MOT (phase M6) to prevent ID swaps.
+4. **17-joint limitation** — COCO keypoints don't cover spine/neck/jaw/fingers; interpolation is required for full rigs.
+5. **SMPL licensing** — WHAM requires SMPL/SMPLify registration, which is a compliance blocker for Phase 4.
+
+## Scope Boundaries (Out of Scope)
+
+- Writing production code (planning only).
+- Creating Blender files (.blend).
+- Installing ML libraries or setting up environments.
+- 3D character generation, facial expression tracking, hand pose tracking, or live camera capture (future extensions).
+
+## Blockers for Execution
+
+1. **Blender version target** — undefined; add-on API compatibility varies across 3.x/4.x.
+2. **Hardware requirements** — no GPU/CPU specification defined.
+3. **Distribution model** — open-source vs. paid release is undecided.
+4. **RTMPose-m vs. RTMO** — not resolved for v1 primary model selection.
+5. **SMPL licensing path** — WHAM integration depends on legal/compliance clearance.

+# Architecture Decision Log
+
+**Source-plan context:** `.pm/PLAN_SUMMARY.md`, `documentation/PLAN.md`, `deep-research-report.md`
+
+---
+
+## ADR-1: Out-of-Process Inference
+
+**Decision:** All ML inference (MMPose, SAM 2, ByteTrack, WHAM) runs as separate Python subprocesses outside Blender's embedded Python.
+
+**Rationale:** Blender ships its own Python distribution. Embedding PyTorch/CUDA inside Blender's environment is complex and fragile. A separate process avoids DLL conflicts, simplifies dependency management, and lets Blender remain stable even if the inference worker crashes.
+
+**Consequences:**
+- Communication must use IPC (cached JSON files are the default).
+- The MMPose worker requires its own Python environment with PyTorch installed.
+- Slightly higher latency for large data transfer, justified by the decoupling benefit.
+
+**Status:** **Accepted** — mandated by all three planning sources.
+
+---
+
+## ADR-2: JSON-First Communication
+
+**Decision:** Data exchange between the MMPose worker and Blender uses cached JSON files, not in-memory pipes or shared libraries.
+
+**Rationale:** JSON files provide a durable, inspectable, and debuggable exchange format. They decouple the inference pipeline from the Blender UI thread. This enables offline processing and re-running steps without re-tracking raw video.
+
+**Consequences:**
+- Requires a defined tracking result schema (BACKLOG item 2.3).
+- File I/O becomes a performance factor — profiled in Phase 9.
+- Parallel workers require unique file paths or lock mechanisms.
+
+**Status:** **Accepted** — mandated by all three planning sources.
+
+---
+
+## ADR-3: MMPose/RTMPose as Primary Backend
+
+**Decision:** MMPose (RTMPose family) is the primary pose estimation backend. SAM 2 and ByteTrack are phase-two additions. LoRATv2 is deprecated for v1.
+
+**Rationale:** LoRATv2 outputs bounding boxes, not pose keypoints. Blender users need skeleton tracking for animation, camera rigging, and retargeting. MMPose provides 17 standard COCO keypoints per person with real-time performance (90+ FPS CPU, 430+ FPS GPU).
+
+**Consequences:**
+- Only 17 body joints are tracked in v1 — spine/neck/jaw/finger bones are interpolated.
+- SAM 2/ByteTrack integration is deferred to phase M6.
+- LoRATv2 may be retained as a camera-solving fallback (bounding boxes for tracking reference).
+
+**Status:** **Accepted** — resolution documented in PLAN_SUMMARY contradiction section.
+
+---
+
+## ADR-4: Empties as v1 Output
+
+**Decision:** Phase 1 output is Blender empties at keypoint positions. Armature retargeting is deferred to phase M5.
+
+**Rationale:** The source plan explicitly lists armature retargeting as Phase 2 (weeks 5–8). Starting with empties provides immediate value (motion paths, visualization) without the complexity of skeleton mapping.
+
+**Consequences:**
+- Users get pose tracks → empties with motion paths in v1.
+- Full animation pipeline requires Phase 2 delivery.
+- The choice of empty vs. armature for v1 is intentional ambiguity (see Unresolved Decisions below).
+
+**Status:** **Accepted** — aligns with phased plan in documentation/PLAN.md.
+
+---
+
+## Unresolved Decisions
+
+### RTMPose-m vs. RTMO for v1
+RTMPose-m has higher COCO AP (75.8); RTMO is faster for multi-person. The source plans do not resolve this. Recommendation: try both during M1 benchmarking (backlog item 1.2).
+
+### Blender version target
+No Blender version is specified in any source plan. Add-on API compatibility (e.g., `bpy.types.Panel` changes between 3.x and 4.x) is a decision that must be made.
+
+### Hardware requirements
+No GPU/CPU requirements are defined. GPU inference needs CUDA-capable hardware; CPU-only targets need RTMPose quantization strategy.
+
+### Distribution model
+Open-source marketplace add-on vs. paid release is undefined. No source plan addresses this.
+
+### SMPL licensing path
+WHAM requires SMPL/SMPLify registration. It is unclear whether a legal/compliance path exists. If blocked, WHAM should be replaced with an alternative (e.g., VideoPose3D).

+# Project Brief — Blender Motion Tracking Enhancement
+
+---
+
+## Purpose
+
+Integrate state-of-the-art human pose tracking into Blender's Video Editor for automatic camera rigging, motion retargeting, and animation. The system takes video input, produces 2D pose tracks with persistent IDs, maps them to Blender empties or armature bones, and optionally lifts to 3D.
+
+## Planning Sources
+
+The project scope is defined by three planning documents:
+
+- **`.pm/PLAN_SUMMARY.md`** — Technical planning summary derived from the master plan and deep research report.
+- **`documentation/PLAN.md`** — 18-week phased implementation plan with milestones and phases.
+- **`deep-research-report.md`** — Comparative analysis of candidate tracking backends (MMPose, SAM 2, ByteTrack, LoRATv2, WHAM).
+
+---
+
+## Recommended Architecture
+
+```
+Video / Still Images
+    → Blender Add-on Panel (launch MMPose worker, configure options)
+        → MMPose Worker (external Python subprocess, RTMPose inference)
+            → 2D Keypoints + Track IDs (cached JSON)
+                → Temporal Smoothing + Gap Fill
+                    → Blender Empties / Armature Bones
+                        → Optional 3D Pose Lift (WHAM, phase-dependent)
+                            → Animation Curves in Scene
+```
+
+## Primary Backend: MMPose / RTMPose
+
+MMPose with RTMPose is the recommended v1 backend. It produces 2D keypoints directly mappable to Blender bones and empties, with real-time performance (90+ FPS on CPU, 430+ FPS on GPU) and an Apache-2.0 license.
+
+## Target Phases
+
+1. **MMPose Integration** (Weeks 1–4): Video → MMPose → empties with keypoints + track IDs.
+2. **Armature Retargeting** (Weeks 5–8): Skeleton bone mapping, automatic armature generation, animation curves.
+3. **Multi-Person + Object Tracking** (Weeks 9–12): SAM 2, ByteTrack, RTMO integration.
+4. **3D Pose Lifting** (Weeks 13–15): Optional 2D→3D lift via WHAM.
+5. **Optimization & Polish** (Weeks 16–18): Latency optimization, TensorRT, UI polish, documentation.
+
+## Why Heavy ML Inference Runs Outside Blender (v1)
+
+Blender ships its own bundled Python distribution. Embedding PyTorch and CUDA inside Blender's Python environment introduces significant complexity:
+
+- **Dependency conflicts:** Blender's Python has its own version and bundled packages. Adding PyTorch (1200+ MB) and CUDA toolkits risks DLL conflicts.
+- **Stability:** A crash in the ML worker would take Blender down with it if embedded. Out-of-process keeps Blender stable.
+- **Distribution:** Shipping a combined Blender + PyTorch installer is impractical — PyTorch alone is 1.2+ GB with CUDA dependencies.
+- **Flexibility:** A separate worker lets users upgrade PyTorch independently, supports GPU/CPU toggle, and enables headless operation on a remote machine.
+
+The out-of-process design is mandated by all three planning sources.
+
+## Why Blender Consumes Cached Tracking Outputs
+
+Communication between Blender and the MMPose worker uses cached JSON files — not in-memory pipes or embedded libraries — because:
+
+- **Inspection & debugging:** JSON files are human-readable. Users can inspect tracking results, compare frames, and debug ID switches without rerunning inference.
+- **Idempotency:** Tracking outputs can be cached and reused. Users can tweak visualization, retargeting, or smoothing without re-tracking video.
+- **Decoupling:** The worker and Blender can run independently. The worker can process multiple videos; Blender can import any cached result at any time.
+- **Simplicity:** File-based exchange avoids complex IPC protocols, shared memory, or network sockets.
+
+## Key Constraints
+
+1. **Not a Python project** — deliverable is a Blender add-on, not a standalone Python repo.
+2. **Monocular 3D ambiguity** — 3D pose lifting is optional; depth recovery from a single camera is inherently ambiguous.
+3. **Identity consistency** — crowded scenes require robust MOT (phase M6) to prevent ID swaps.
+4. **17-joint limitation** — COCO keypoints don't cover spine/neck/jaw/fingers; interpolation is required for full rigs.
+5. **SMPL licensing** — WHAM requires SMPL/SMPLify registration, which is a compliance blocker for Phase 4.
+
+## Scope Boundaries (Out of Scope)
+
+- Writing production code (planning only).
+- Creating Blender files (.blend).
+- Installing ML libraries or setting up environments.
+- 3D character generation, facial expression tracking, hand pose tracking, or live camera capture (future extensions).
+
+## Blockers for Execution
+
+1. **Blender version target** — undefined; add-on API compatibility varies across 3.x/4.x.
+2. **Hardware requirements** — no GPU/CPU specification defined.
+3. **Distribution model** — open-source vs. paid release is undecided.
+4. **RTMPose-m vs. RTMO** — not resolved for v1 primary model selection.
+5. **SMPL licensing path** — WHAM integration depends on legal/compliance clearance.

+    "patch": "Index: .pm/DECISIONS.md\n===================================================================\n--- .pm/DECISIONS.md\t\n+++ .pm/DECISIONS.md\t\n@@ -0,0 +1,82 @@\n+# Architecture Decision Log\n+\n+**Source-plan context:** `.pm/PLAN_SUMMARY.md`, `documentation/PLAN.md`, `deep-research-report.md`\n+\n+---\n+\n+## ADR-1: Out-of-Process Inference\n+\n+**Decision:** All ML inference (MMPose, SAM 2, ByteTrack, WHAM) runs as separate Python subprocesses outside Blender's embedded Python.\n+\n+**Rationale:** Blender ships its own Python distribution. Embedding PyTorch/CUDA inside Blender's environment is complex and fragile. A separate process avoids DLL conflicts, simplifies dependency management, and lets Blender remain stable even if the inference worker crashes.\n+\n+**Consequences:**\n+- Communication must use IPC (cached JSON files are the default).\n+- The MMPose worker requires its own Python environment with PyTorch installed.\n+- Slightly higher latency for large data transfer, justified by the decoupling benefit.\n+\n+**Status:** **Accepted** — mandated by all three planning sources.\n+\n+---\n+\n+## ADR-2: JSON-First Communication\n+\n+**Decision:** Data exchange between the MMPose worker and Blender uses cached JSON files, not in-memory pipes or shared libraries.\n+\n+**Rationale:** JSON files provide a durable, inspectable, and debuggable exchange format. They decouple the inference pipeline from the Blender UI thread. This enables offline processing and re-running steps without re-tracking raw video.\n+\n+**Consequences:**\n+- Requires a defined tracking result schema (BACKLOG item 2.3).\n+- File I/O becomes a performance factor — profiled in Phase 9.\n+- Parallel workers require unique file paths or lock mechanisms.\n+\n+**Status:** **Accepted** — mandated by all three planning sources.\n+\n+---\n+\n+## ADR-3: MMPose/RTMPose as Primary Backend\n+\n+**Decision:** MMPose (RTMPose family) is the primary pose estimation backend. SAM 2 and ByteTrack are phase-two additions. LoRATv2 is deprecated for v1.\n+\n+**Rationale:** LoRATv2 outputs bounding boxes, not pose keypoints. Blender users need skeleton tracking for animation, camera rigging, and retargeting. MMPose provides 17 standard COCO keypoints per person with real-time performance (90+ FPS CPU, 430+ FPS GPU).\n+\n+**Consequences:**\n+- Only 17 body joints are tracked in v1 — spine/neck/jaw/finger bones are interpolated.\n+- SAM 2/ByteTrack integration is deferred to phase M6.\n+- LoRATv2 may be retained as a camera-solving fallback (bounding boxes for tracking reference).\n+\n+**Status:** **Accepted** — resolution documented in PLAN_SUMMARY contradiction section.\n+\n+---\n+\n+## ADR-4: Empties as v1 Output\n+\n+**Decision:** Phase 1 output is Blender empties at keypoint positions. Armature retargeting is deferred to phase M5.\n+\n+**Rationale:** The source plan explicitly lists armature retargeting as Phase 2 (weeks 5–8). Starting with empties provides immediate value (motion paths, visualization) without the complexity of skeleton mapping.\n+\n+**Consequences:**\n+- Users get pose tracks → empties with motion paths in v1.\n+- Full animation pipeline requires Phase 2 delivery.\n+- The choice of empty vs. armature for v1 is intentional ambiguity (see Unresolved Decisions below).\n+\n+**Status:** **Accepted** — aligns with phased plan in documentation/PLAN.md.\n+\n+---\n+\n+## Unresolved Decisions\n+\n+### RTMPose-m vs. RTMO for v1\n+RTMPose-m has higher COCO AP (75.8); RTMO is faster for multi-person. The source plans do not resolve this. Recommendation: try both during M1 benchmarking (backlog item 1.2).\n+\n+### Blender version target\n+No Blender version is specified in any source plan. Add-on API compatibility (e.g., `bpy.types.Panel` changes between 3.x and 4.x) is a decision that must be made.\n+\n+### Hardware requirements\n+No GPU/CPU requirements are defined. GPU inference needs CUDA-capable hardware; CPU-only targets need RTMPose quantization strategy.\n+\n+### Distribution model\n+Open-source marketplace add-on vs. paid release is undefined. No source plan addresses this.\n+\n+### SMPL licensing path\n+WHAM requires SMPL/SMPLify registration. It is unclear whether a legal/compliance path exists. If blocked, WHAM should be replaced with an alternative (e.g., VideoPose3D).\n",

+    "file": ".pm/PROJECT_BRIEF.md",
+    "patch": "Index: .pm/PROJECT_BRIEF.md\n===================================================================\n--- .pm/PROJECT_BRIEF.md\t\n+++ .pm/PROJECT_BRIEF.md\t\n@@ -1,16 +1,85 @@\n-# Project Brief\r\n-\r\n-Goal: Build a Blender add-on that uses modern motion tracking / pose estimation code to convert video into usable Blender animation data.\r\n-\r\n-Initial technical direction:\r\n-- Use MMPose / RTMPose as the first backend.\r\n-- Run inference outside Blender.\r\n-- Cache results as JSON.\r\n-- Import tracked keypoints into Blender as empties, curves, or armature controls.\r\n-- Avoid embedding PyTorch directly into Blender for v1.\r\n-\r\n-Constraints:\r\n-- Work in small, reviewable tasks.\r\n-- Every task must include tests or a manual validation step.\r\n-- Do not make broad refactors unless the task explicitly requests them.\r\n-- Prefer simple, inspectable code over clever automation.\n\\ No newline at end of file\n+# Project Brief — Blender Motion Tracking Enhancement\n+\n+---\n+\n+## Purpose\n+\n+Integrate state-of-the-art human pose tracking into Blender's Video Editor for automatic camera rigging, motion retargeting, and animation. The system takes video input, produces 2D pose tracks with persistent IDs, maps them to Blender empties or armature bones, and optionally lifts to 3D.\n+\n+## Planning Sources\n+\n+The project scope is defined by three planning documents:\n+\n+- **`.pm/PLAN_SUMMARY.md`** — Technical planning summary derived from the master plan and deep research report.\n+- **`documentation/PLAN.md`** — 18-week phased implementation plan with milestones and phases.\n+- **`deep-research-report.md`** — Comparative analysis of candidate tracking backends (MMPose, SAM 2, ByteTrack, LoRATv2, WHAM).\n+\n+---\n+\n+## Recommended Architecture\n+\n+```\n+Video / Still Images\n+    → Blender Add-on Panel (launch MMPose worker, configure options)\n+        → MMPose Worker (external Python subprocess, RTMPose inference)\n+            → 2D Keypoints + Track IDs (cached JSON)\n+                → Temporal Smoothing + Gap Fill\n+                    → Blender Empties / Armature Bones\n+                        → Optional 3D Pose Lift (WHAM, phase-dependent)\n+                            → Animation Curves in Scene\n+```\n+\n+## Primary Backend: MMPose / RTMPose\n+\n+MMPose with RTMPose is the recommended v1 backend. It produces 2D keypoints directly mappable to Blender bones and empties, with real-time performance (90+ FPS on CPU, 430+ FPS on GPU) and an Apache-2.0 license.\n+\n+## Target Phases\n+\n+1. **MMPose Integration** (Weeks 1–4): Video → MMPose → empties with keypoints + track IDs.\n+2. **Armature Retargeting** (Weeks 5–8): Skeleton bone mapping, automatic armature generation, animation curves.\n+3. **Multi-Person + Object Tracking** (Weeks 9–12): SAM 2, ByteTrack, RTMO integration.\n+4. **3D Pose Lifting** (Weeks 13–15): Optional 2D→3D lift via WHAM.\n+5. **Optimization & Polish** (Weeks 16–18): Latency optimization, TensorRT, UI polish, documentation.\n+\n+## Why Heavy ML Inference Runs Outside Blender (v1)\n+\n+Blender ships its own bundled Python distribution. Embedding PyTorch and CUDA inside Blender's Python environment introduces significant complexity:\n+\n+- **Dependency conflicts:** Blender's Python has its own version and bundled packages. Adding PyTorch (1200+ MB) and CUDA toolkits risks DLL conflicts.\n+- **Stability:** A crash in the ML worker would take Blender down with it if embedded. Out-of-process keeps Blender stable.\n+- **Distribution:** Shipping a combined Blender + PyTorch installer is impractical — PyTorch alone is 1.2+ GB with CUDA dependencies.\n+- **Flexibility:** A separate worker lets users upgrade PyTorch independently, supports GPU/CPU toggle, and enables headless operation on a remote machine.\n+\n+The out-of-process design is mandated by all three planning sources.\n+\n+## Why Blender Consumes Cached Tracking Outputs\n+\n+Communication between Blender and the MMPose worker uses cached JSON files — not in-memory pipes or embedded libraries — because:\n+\n+- **Inspection & debugging:** JSON files are human-readable. Users can inspect tracking results, compare frames, and debug ID switches without rerunning inference.\n+- **Idempotency:** Tracking outputs can be cached and reused. Users can tweak visualization, retargeting, or smoothing without re-tracking video.\n+- **Decoupling:** The worker and Blender can run independently. The worker can process multiple videos; Blender can import any cached result at any time.\n+- **Simplicity:** File-based exchange avoids complex IPC protocols, shared memory, or network sockets.\n+\n+## Key Constraints\n+\n+1. **Not a Python project** — deliverable is a Blender add-on, not a standalone Python repo.\n+2. **Monocular 3D ambiguity** — 3D pose lifting is optional; depth recovery from a single camera is inherently ambiguous.\n+3. **Identity consistency** — crowded scenes require robust MOT (phase M6) to prevent ID swaps.\n+4. **17-joint limitation** — COCO keypoints don't cover spine/neck/jaw/fingers; interpolation is required for full rigs.\n+5. **SMPL licensing** — WHAM requires SMPL/SMPLify registration, which is a compliance blocker for Phase 4.\n+\n+## Scope Boundaries (Out of Scope)\n+\n+- Writing production code (planning only).\n+- Creating Blender files (.blend).\n+- Installing ML libraries or setting up environments.\n+- 3D character generation, facial expression tracking, hand pose tracking, or live camera capture (future extensions).\n+\n+## Blockers for Execution\n+\n+1. **Blender version target** — undefined; add-on API compatibility varies across 3.x/4.x.\n+2. **Hardware requirements** — no GPU/CPU specification defined.\n+3. **Distribution model** — open-source vs. paid release is undecided.\n+4. **RTMPose-m vs. RTMO** — not resolved for v1 primary model selection.\n+5. **SMPL licensing path** — WHAM integration depends on legal/compliance clearance.\n",

1: # Technical Planning Summary — Blender Motion Tracking
2: 
3: **Generated from:** `documentation/PLAN.md` + `deep-research-report.md`
4: **Date:** May 2026
5: 
6: ---
7: 
8: ## Core Project Goal
9: 
10: Integrate state-of-the-art human pose tracking into Blender's Video Editor for automatic camera rigging, motion retargeting, and animation. The system takes video input, produces 2D pose tracks with persistent IDs, maps them to Blender empties or armature bones, and optionally lifts to 3D.
11: 
12: ---
13: 
14: ## Recommended SOTA Tracking Backend
15: 
16: **MMPose / RTMPose** is the recommended primary backend for v1.
17: 
18: | Metric | Value |
19: |---|---|
20: | COCO AP (RTMPose-m) | 75.8 |
21: | CPU throughput | 90+ FPS (i7-11700) |
22: | GPU throughput | 430+ FPS (GTX 1660 Ti) |
23: | License | Apache-2.0 |
24: | Keypoints | 17 standard COCO body joints per person |
25: 
26: **Justification:** MMPose produces 2D keypoints directly mappable to Blender bones/empties. LoRATv2 outputs bounding boxes, which are not animation-ready. MMPose's real-time performance, permissive license, and成熟的 ecosystem make it the best v1 fit.
27: 
28: **Phase-two backends:** SAM 2 (promptable object masks), ByteTrack (general MOT), RTMO (multi-person).
29: 
30: ---
31: 
32: ## Proposed Blender Integration Architecture
33: 
34: ```
35: Video/Still Images
36:     → Blender Add-on Panel (launch MMPose worker)
37:         → MMPose Inference (RTMPose/RTMO)
38:             → 2D Keypoints + Track IDs (JSON cache)
39:                 → Temporal Smoothing + Gap Fill
40:                     → Blender Empties / Armature Bones
41:                         → Optional 3D Pose Lift (WHAM)
42:                             → Animation Curves in Scene
43: ```
44: 
45: **Key design decision:** All inference runs **out of process**. Blender spawns a Python subprocess with its own PyTorch environment. Communication is via cached JSON files, not embedded libraries.
46: 
47: ---
48: 
49: ## Key Constraints
50: 
51: 1. **Not a Python project** — deliverable is a Blender add-on, not a standalone Python repo.
52: 2. **Out-of-process inference** — PyTorch/CUDA must run in a separate process from Blender's bundled Python.
53: 3. **JSON-first communication** — frame-to-frame data exchange via cached JSON files.
54: 4. **Monocular 3D ambiguity** — 3D pose lifting is optional; depth recovery from a single camera is inherently ambiguous.
55: 5. **SMPL licensing** — WHAM requires SMPL/SMPLify registration, adding complexity for 3D phase.
56: 6. **Identity consistency** — crowded scenes require robust MOT to prevent ID swaps.
57: 
58: ---
59: 
60: ## Major Phases
61: 
62: | Phase | Weeks | Objective | Key Deliverable |
63: |---|---|---|---|
64: | **1** | 1-4 | MMPose integration | Blender add-on: video → MMPose → empties with keypoints + IDs |
65: | **2** | 5-8 | Armature retargeting | Skeleton bone mapping (17 joints → rig), automatic armature generation |
66: | **3** | 9-12 | Multi-person + objects | SAM 2, RTMO, ByteTrack integration for crowded scenes |
67: | **4** | 13-15 | 3D pose lifting | Optional WHAM-based 2D→3D lift, world-space positioning |
68: | **5** | 16-18 | Optimization & polish | <50ms latency, TensorRT, UI polish, documentation |
69: 
70: ---
71: 
72: ## Highest-Risk Assumptions
73: 
74: 1. **MMPose keypoints map cleanly to common Blender rigs** (Humanoid, Rigify, Mixamo). Gaps exist for spine/neck/jaw/fingers beyond 17 COCO joints — mitigation: interpolation + user-defined bone mapping.
75: 2. **Out-of-process JSON communication is fast enough** for practical workflows. Mitigation: optimize caching, profile end-to-end latency in Phase 5.
76: 3. **Monocular 3D lifting produces usable results** without manual correction. Mitigation: keep 3D optional, offer manual correction tools.
77: 4. **Multi-person ID stability** holds in real-world crowded footage. Mitigation: RTMO one-stage pipeline + ByteTrack fallback + visual ID labels.
78: 
79: ---
80: 
81: ## Immediate Next Steps
82: 
83: 1. Set up Python environment with MMPose, RTMPose, RTMO, ONNX export.
84: 2. Build external MMPose worker (subprocess from Blender Python).
85: 3. Implement video-to-JSON inference pipeline.
86: 4. Create Blender add-on panel (video input, person selection, output mode).
87: 5. Map MMPose keypoints to Blender empties at joint positions.
88: 
89: ---
90: 
91: ## Contradictions, Gaps, and Unresolved Decisions
92: 
93: ### Contradiction: Original LoRATv2 vs. Current MMPose Plan
94: 
95: The repo's AGENTS.md and initial PLAN_SUMMARY referenced **LoRATv2 + PrTrack + ProMotion** as the target architecture. The deep research and updated PLAN.md have **retconned to MMPose/RTMPose** as the primary backend. This is documented in PLAN.md section "Why MMPose / RTMPose (Not LoRATv2)?": LoRATv2 outputs bounding boxes, not pose keypoints suitable for animation. **Resolution:** MMPose is now the official direction; LoRATv2 is deprecated for v1 (backup for camera solving only).
96: 
97: ### Gaps
98: 
99: 1. **No Blender version target specified** — add-on API compatibility varies by Blender version. Decision needed.
100: 2. **No hardware requirements defined** — GPU inference needs CUDA-capable hardware; CPU-only targets need RTMPose quantization strategy.
101: 3. **No distribution model** — is this an open-source Blender marketplace add-on, Gumroad paid, or free GitHub release?
102: 4. **No timeline for Phase 2-5** — only Phase 1 (weeks 1-4) has a concrete start date.
103: 
104: ### Unresolved Decisions
105: 
106: 1. **RTMPose vs. RTMO for v1** — RTMPose-m has higher accuracy; RTMO is faster for multi-person. Default not specified.
107: 2. **Empty vs. Armature as v1 output** — PLAN.md lists both but Phase 1 deliverable emphasizes empties; armature retargeting is Phase 2. Unclear if v1 should include basic armature mapping.
108: 3. **SMPL licensing path** — WHAM requires SMPL registration. Is there a legal/compliance path for this?
109: 4. **3D lifting: WHAM vs. alternative** — WHAM is strongest but licensing-dependent. Alternatives like VideoPose3D not evaluated.

(End of file - total 109 lines)
</content>

<content>
1: # Blender Motion Tracking Enhancement — Long-Term Implementation Plan
2: 
3: **Goal:** Integrate state-of-the-art human pose tracking into Blender's Video Editor for automatic camera rigging, motion retargeting, and animation.
4: 
5: ---
6: 
7: ## 📋 Table of Contents
8: 
9: 1. [Project Overview](#project-overview)
10: 2. [Core Architecture](#core-architecture)
11: 3. [Phased Implementation Plan](#phased-implementation-plan)
12: 4. [Technical Challenges & Mitigations](#technical-challenges--mitigations)
13: 5. [Milestones & Deliverables](#milestones--deliverables)
14: 6. [Future Extensions](#future-extensions)
15: 
16: ---
17: 
18: ## Project Overview
19: 
20: ### Why MMPose / RTMPose (Not LoRATv2)?
21: 
22: The deep research assessment found that **LoRATv2 outputs bounding boxes**, which are not directly useful for Blender's primary workflows: camera rigging, mocap, and animation retargeting. Blender users need **pose/keypoint tracking** that maps to skeletons, bones, and empties.
23: 
24: **MMPose / RTMPose is recommended** because it produces 2D keypoints directly mapable to Blender, with real-time performance (90+ FPS CPU, 430+ FPS GPU), Apache-2.0 license, and mature ecosystem.
25: 
26: ### Current State
27: Blender's motion tracker places 2D anchor points and follows them for camera solving. It lacks:
28: - Pose/skeleton tracking for animation
29: - Multi-person identity consistency
30: - Motion retargeting to armatures
31: - Automatic rigging
32: 
33: ### Target State
34: A pose-tracking pipeline producing:
35: - Keyframes from 2D pose tracks
36: - Retargeted armature bones from skeletal data
37: - Empties at joint positions with motion paths
38: - Smoothed, gap-filled motion for animation
39: 
40: ### Key Success Metrics
41: | Metric | Target |
42: |--------|--------|
43: | Real-time inference (MMPose) | 90+ FPS CPU (RTMPose) |
44: | Multi-person stable IDs | 100% ID consistency |
45: | Pose accuracy (AP on COCO) | 75.8+ (RTMPose-m) |
46: | Blender empty/retarget mapping | Automatic |
47: | Pose lifting (phase 2) | Optional 2D→3D |
48: 
49: ---
50: 
51: ## Core Architecture
52: 
53: ```
54: Blender Motion Tracking Add-on (NEW)
55: ├── Phase 1: MMPose / RTMPose (2D pose + track IDs)
56: ├── Phase 2: SAM 2 + ByteTrack (object masks + MOT)
57: ├── Phase 3: WHAM (world-space 3D pose lift)
58: ├── MMPose Worker: External process (not embedded)
59: ├── JSON Cache: Keypoints + IDs between frames
60: ├── Temporal Smoothing: Gap fill + interpolation
61: ├── Blender Output: Empties + Armature mapping
62: └── Optional: 3D pose lift → animation curves
63: ```
64: 
65: ```
66: Video/Still Images
67:     → Blender Add-on Panel (launch MMPose worker)
68:         → MMPose Inference (RTMPose/RTMO)
69:             → 2D Keypoints + Track IDs (JSON cache)
70:                 → Temporal Smoothing + Gap Fill
71:                     → Blender Empties / Armature Bones
72:                         → Optional 3D Pose Lift (WHAM)
73:                             → Animation Curves in Scene
74: ```
75: 
76: ---
77: 
78: ## Phased Implementation Plan
79: 
80: ### Phase 1: MMPose Integration (Weeks 1-4)
81: **Objective:** Build Blender add-on that runs MMPose externally and maps 2D pose tracks to empties.
82: 
83: **Tasks:**
84: - [ ] Set up Python environment with MMPose, RTMPose, RTMO, ONNX export
85: - [ ] Build external MMPose worker (subprocess from Blender Python)
86: - [ ] Implement video-to-JSON inference pipeline (MMPose inferencer → cached JSON)
87: - [ ] Create Blender add-on panel: video input, person selection, output mode
88: - [ ] Map MMPose keypoints to Blender empties at joint positions
89: - [ ] Add track ID visualization in Blender viewport
90: - [ ] Implement basic temporal smoothing on empty positions between frames
91: 
92: **Deliverables:**
93: - Working Blender add-on that accepts video, runs MMPose, creates empties
94: - Keypoints at all 17 standard body joints per person
95: - Persistent track IDs across frames
96: - Basic motion path display in 3D viewport
97: 
98: ---
99: 
100: ### Phase 2: Armature Retargeting (Weeks 5-8)
101: **Objective:** Map pose tracks to Blender armature bones for animation retargeting.
102: 
103: **Tasks:**
104: - [ ] Implement skeleton bone mapping (MMPose 17 joints → Blender rig structure)
105: - [ ] Create automatic armature generation from pose tracks
106: - [ ] Add IK/FK retargeting options (user selects preferred rig type)
107: - [ ] Implement animation curve generation from pose keyframes
108: - [ ] Add gap-filling for occluded frames (interpolation/ML fill)
109: - [ ] Polish UI: retarget mode selector, bone mapping config
110: - [ ] Test on diverse body types and poses
111: 
112: **Deliverables:**
113: - Automatic armature retargeting pipeline
114: - Animation curves populated from pose tracks
115: - Gap-filled motion for 50+ frame occlusions
116: - Retarget UI matching Blender's standard animation workflow
117: 
118: ---
119: 
120: ### Phase 3: Multi-Person + Object Tracking (Weeks 9-12)
121: **Objective:** Add SAM 2 for object tracking and ByteTrack for MOT support.
122: 
123: **Tasks:**
124: - [ ] Integrate SAM 2: promptable object masks for props/subjects
125: - [ ] Integrate RTMO for multi-person tracking (crowded scenes)
126: - [ ] Add ByteTrack: general object MOT backend (for non-human objects)
127: - [ ] Implement SAM 2 + MMPose pipeline (SAM finds person, MMPose tracks pose)
128: - [ ] Add object mask overlays to Blender (for compositing/matte generation)
129: - [ ] Support empty + armature creation for multiple subjects simultaneously
130: 
131: **Deliverables:**
132: - Multi-person tracking with stable IDs
133: - SAM 2 promptable object tracking for props/subjects
134: - ByteTrack MOT support for general objects
135: - Automatic creation of N armatures in crowded scene
136: 
137: ---
138: 
139: ### Phase 4: 3D Pose Lifting (Weeks 13-15)
140: **Objective:** Add optional 2D→3D pose lifting using WHAM or similar.
141: 
142: **Tasks:**
143: - [ ] Evaluate WHAM for Blender integration (SMPL licensing check)
144: - [ ] Implement optional 3D pose lift from MMPose 2D keypoints
145: - [ ] Add camera-relative → world-space transform
146: - [ ] Test on challenging camera motions (fast pans, zooms)
147: - [ ] Add fallback to 2D-only when 3D fails
148: 
149: **Deliverables:**
150: - Optional 3D pose output alongside 2D tracks
151: - World-space positioning in Blender scene
152: - Working 3D armatures for motion capture
153: 
154: ---
155: 
156: ### Phase 5: Optimization & Polish (Weeks 16-18)
157: **Objective:** Achieve target performance, polish UI, documentation.
158: 
159: **Tasks:**
160: - [ ] Profile inference pipeline end-to-end (Blender → MMPose → Blender)
161: - [ ] Optimize JSON caching and communication between processes
162: - [ ] Add ONNX export of RTMPose for faster inference
163: - [ ] Add TensorRT backend for GPU optimization
164: - [ ] Polish Blender UI: tooltips, presets, keyboard shortcuts
165: - [ ] Testing: 50+ diverse video sequences
166: - [ ] Documentation, tutorials, demo reel
167: 
168: **Deliverables:**
169: - <50ms round-trip latency (video → Blender empties)
170: - Real-time playback during inference
171: - User-tested, polished add-on
172: - Documentation and video demos
173: 
174: ---
175: 
176: ## Technical Challenges & Mitigations
177: 
178: ### Challenge 1: PyTorch/CUDA Packaging Around Blender
179: **Problem:** Blender ships its own Python; adding a separate PyTorch/CUDA stack is complex.
180: **Mitigation:** Run MMPose **out-of-process**. Blender spawns a Python subprocess with its own PyTorch environment. No embedding of PyTorch into Blender. Use JSON file caching for frame-to-frame communication.
181: 
182: ### Challenge 2: Identity Consistency in Crowded Scenes
183: **Problem:** Multiple people moving past each other — IDs can swap.
184: **Mitigation:** RTMO handles identity in one-stage pipeline (reduces ID switches). Fallback to ByteTrack for general MOT. Add visual ID labels in Blender UI.
185: 
186: ### Challenge 3: Camera-Relative vs World-Space 3D
187: **Problem:** Monocular 3D pose lifting has depth ambiguity.
188: **Mitigation:** Keep 3D lifting optional. Use SMPL parameters as a guide, not definitive truth. Offer manual correction tools in Blender. WHAM's world-space recovery handles this better but requires SLAM.
189: 
190: ### Challenge 4: Pose to Armature Mapping Complexity
191: **Problem:** 17 standard keypoints don't fully map to production rigs (spine, neck, jaw, fingers).
192: **Mitigation:** Interpolate missing bones from nearby keypoints. Allow user-defined bone mapping. Provide presets for common rig types (Humanoid, Rigify, Mixamo).
193: 
194: ---
195: 
196: ## Milestones & Deliverables
197: 
198: | Week | Milestone | Deliverable |
199: |------|-----------|-------------|
200: | 4 | MMPose working | Pose tracks → empties in Blender |
201: | 8 | Armature retargeting | Automatic rig mapping + animation |

1: # Blender Motion Tracking Integration Recommendation
2: 
3: ## Executive Summary
4: 
5: My recommendation is to integrate urlMMPose repoturn2search0 first, using the RTMPose/RTMO family as the backbone for a new Blender motion-tracking workflow. Among current open-source options, it has the best balance of recent benchmark strength, real-time deployment paths, permissive licensing, mature documentation, and Blender-friendly outputs. In practice, MMPose can take images, videos, folders, or webcam streams; emit structured keypoints and saved JSON predictions; and support pose visualization, tracking-aware 3D pose lifting, and export to ONNX/TensorRT through its documented deployment stack. RTMPose-m reports 75.8 AP on COCO with 90+ FPS on an Intel i7-11700 CPU and 430+ FPS on a GTX 1660 Ti, and MMPose’s RTMO release targets crowded multi-person scenes as a real-time one-stage method. That combination is unusually well aligned with what Blender users actually need: stable body/whole-body tracks that can become empties, bones, or retargeted armatures rather than just boxes or masks. citeturn6search15turn12view1turn11search7turn10view1turn9view0turn3search9turn23search0turn23search7
6: 
7: The runner-up choices are strong in narrower lanes, not as first integration targets. urlSAM 2 repoturn2search3 is the best option for promptable video masks and object roto/tracking; urlByteTrack repoturn2search1 remains the most practical open MOT backend; urlLoRAT repoturn2search18 is the most relevant recent single-object tracker from Heng Fan’s publication list; and urlWHAM repoturn4search2 is the strongest human-motion-recovery candidate when global/world-grounded motion matters. But each of those imposes more post-processing or narrower scope for a Blender v1 than MMPose does. My implementation estimate is **medium** for a useful v1 built on MMPose, and **high** for a polished full system with robust 3D retargeting and world-space recovery. citeturn16view2turn16view4turn8view1turn19search6turn6search2turn24view4
8: 
9: ## Research Landscape
10: 
11: Over the last three years, the motion-tracking frontier has split into five distinct lanes: strong single-object tracking with transformer backbones, real-time multi-object tracking by better association, promptable video object segmentation/tracking, real-time human pose estimation/tracking, and world-grounded human motion recovery. Heng Fan’s recent publication stream is especially relevant because it reflects exactly where tracking research is moving now: category-general SOT and benchmark scaling via urlVastTrack benchmarkturn3search3, language-guided MOT via urlLaMOT benchmarkturn3search2, and parameter-efficient transformer tracking via urlLoRAT repoturn2search18; on the same publications page, titles such as *Beyond MOT* and *ProMotion* reinforce the shift toward semantic, language-guided, and motion-aware formulations rather than small closed-set tracking setups. citeturn1view0turn3search6turn3search7turn19search6
12: 
13: The uploaded 2022 LSTM-motion-model paper is still useful historical context because it improved legacy trackers such as GOTURN, SiamFC, and DiMP by making their search regions motion-aware, but I would treat it as a baseline concept rather than a 2026 integration target. fileciteturn0file0
14: 
15: ## Candidate Comparison
16: 
17: | Candidate | What it gives Blender | Key facts | Integration verdict | Evidence |
18: |---|---|---|---|---|
19: | urlMMPose repoturn2search0 · urlRTMPose paperturn6search15 | Human/body/whole-body pose tracking; optional 2D→3D pipeline; JSON-first outputs | RTMPose-m: 75.8 AP on COCO, 90+ FPS CPU, 430+ FPS GPU; MMPose inferencer accepts image/video/webcam and saves JSON; docs cover ONNX/TensorRT export; Python 3.7+, PyTorch 1.8+, CUDA 9.2+; Apache-2.0; 7.6k stars and 35 releases. | **Recommended.** Best Blender v1 because keypoints and skeletons are directly useful for rigs, motion paths, and animation overlays. **Effort:** medium. **Main blockers:** retargeting, smoothing, monocular depth ambiguity. | Official repo, paper, docs, and release notes. citeturn6search15turn12view1turn11search7turn10view1turn11search6turn9view0turn3search9 |
20: | urlSAM 2 repoturn2search3 · urlSAM 2 paperturn7search3 | Promptable object masks and video propagation for arbitrary props/subjects | SAM 2.1 large reports 79.5 J&F on SA-V, 74.6 on MOSE, 80.6 on LVOS v2 at 39.5 FPS on A100; API supports adding prompts and propagating masklets through video for multiple objects; Python ≥3.10, torch ≥2.5.1, optional CUDA extension; Apache-2.0 plus BSD-3-Clause components; 19.1k stars. | Best **phase-two** backend if the design goal becomes object masks/roto, not animation-ready skeletons. **Effort:** medium. **Main blockers:** prompt UX, mask-to-track conversion, GPU-first packaging. | Official repo, checkpoints table, and install/API docs. citeturn16view1turn16view2turn16view3turn16view4turn9view3turn21view0 |

Runtime is not clearly specified in official repo/project materials. | Strong research candidate for a later “video-to-mocap” module, not the best first Blender integration. **Effort:** high. **Main blockers:** SMPL licensing/registration, SLAM robustness, and retargeting from recovered body model to production rigs. | Official project and repo documentation. citeturn6search2turn8view5turn24view3turn24view4turn21view3 |
24: 
25: ## Recommended Integration Approach
26: 
27: The best first integration target is MMPose from entity["organization","OpenMMLab","computer vision toolkit"], implemented as a Blender add-on that runs inference **out of process** and exchanges cached JSON/video outputs with Blender rather than embedding the full training/runtime stack into Blender’s bundled Python immediately. That design matches both the documented MMPose inferencer workflow and Blender’s Python extension model: MMPose already supports saved predictions, videos, and programmatic APIs, while Blender’s official Python API is designed to script animation, import/export, and scene data manipulation. In practical terms, v1 should use RTMPose/RTMO for 2D pose tracks, expose smoothing/gap-fill options, and retarget the resulting tracks to empties or armature controls; the 3D pose-lifter can be added as an optional second stage once 2D tracking is stable. If later needed, keep adapters ready for SAM 2 and ByteTrack as alternate backends rather than trying to make one model solve every lane on day one. citeturn12view1turn10view1turn23search0turn23search7turn23search8
28: 
29: A compact integration flow consistent with the documented APIs is:
30: 
31: ```mermaid
32: flowchart LR
33:     A[Video or image sequence] --> B[Blender add-on panel]
34:     B --> C[External MMPose worker]
35:     C --> D[2D keypoints and track IDs JSON cache]
36:     D --> E[Temporal smoothing and gap fill]
37:     E --> F[Blender empties or armature mapping]
38:     F --> G[Optional 3D pose lift]
39:     G --> H[Animation curves in scene]
40: ```
41: 
42: This flow is feasible because MMPose already supports image/video inference and persistent prediction outputs, while Blender exposes the Python hooks needed to create and animate scene objects from those outputs. citeturn12view1turn23search0turn23search7
43: 
44: ## Effort and Blockers
45: 
46: My engineering estimate is **medium** for a useful first release built on MMPose: 2D pose tracking, cached JSON outputs, visual overlays, and basic armature/empty retargeting are all supported by the existing MMPose and Blender API surfaces. The jump to a polished production system is **high** because the real complexity is not inference alone; it is temporal stabilization, identity consistency in crowded scenes, rig retargeting, and monocular 3D ambiguity. The biggest concrete blocker for the recommended path is packaging PyTorch/CUDA cleanly around Blender; the biggest blocker for the motion-capture alternatives is additional model-ecosystem friction, especially WHAM’s documented SMPL/SMPLify registration requirements and the increase in camera/SLAM complexity. That is why MMPose is the right first bet: it minimizes licensing friction and post-processing cost while producing the most immediately useful Blender-native representation. citeturn11search6turn10view1turn23search0turn24view4turn16view4

## Dependencies & Blockers

- Phase M6 (SAM 2, ByteTrack) depends on Phase M5 stabilizing first.
- Phase M8 (3D lifting) is blocked until SMPL licensing is resolved.
- Hardware requirements are undefined — no target GPU/CPU specification in source plans.

# Architecture Decision Log

**Source-plan context:** `.pm/PLAN_SUMMARY.md`, `documentation/PLAN.md`, `deep-research-report.md`

---

## ADR-1: Out-of-Process Inference

**Decision:** All ML inference (MMPose, SAM 2, ByteTrack, WHAM) runs as separate Python subprocesses outside Blender's embedded Python.

**Rationale:** Blender ships its own Python distribution. Embedding PyTorch/CUDA inside Blender's environment is complex and fragile. A separate process avoids DLL conflicts, simplifies dependency management, and lets Blender remain stable even if the inference worker crashes.

**Consequences:**
- Communication must use IPC (cached JSON files are the default).
- The MMPose worker requires its own Python environment with PyTorch installed.
- Slightly higher latency for large data transfer, justified by the decoupling benefit.

**Status:** **Accepted** — mandated by all three planning sources.

---

## ADR-2: JSON-First Communication

**Decision:** Data exchange between the MMPose worker and Blender uses cached JSON files, not in-memory pipes or shared libraries.

**Rationale:** JSON files provide a durable, inspectable, and debuggable exchange format. They decouple the inference pipeline from the Blender UI thread. This enables offline processing and re-running steps without re-tracking raw video.

**Consequences:**
- Requires a defined tracking result schema (BACKLOG item 2.3).
- File I/O becomes a performance factor — profiled in Phase 9.
- Parallel workers require unique file paths or lock mechanisms.

**Status:** **Accepted** — mandated by all three planning sources.

---

## ADR-3: MMPose/RTMPose as Primary Backend

**Decision:** MMPose (RTMPose family) is the primary pose estimation backend. SAM 2 and ByteTrack are phase-two additions. LoRATv2 is deprecated for v1.

**Rationale:** LoRATv2 outputs bounding boxes, not pose keypoints. Blender users need skeleton tracking for animation, camera rigging, and retargeting. MMPose provides 17 standard COCO keypoints per person with real-time performance (90+ FPS CPU, 430+ FPS GPU).

**Consequences:**
- Only 17 body joints are tracked in v1 — spine/neck/jaw/finger bones are interpolated.
- SAM 2/ByteTrack integration is deferred to phase M6.
- LoRATv2 may be retained as a camera-solving fallback (bounding boxes for tracking reference).

**Status:** **Accepted** — resolution documented in PLAN_SUMMARY contradiction section.

---

## ADR-4: Empties as v1 Output

**Decision:** Phase 1 output is Blender empties at keypoint positions. Armature retargeting is deferred to phase M5.

**Rationale:** The source plan explicitly lists armature retargeting as Phase 2 (weeks 5–8). Starting with empties provides immediate value (motion paths, visualization) without the complexity of skeleton mapping.

**Consequences:**
- Users get pose tracks → empties with motion paths in v1.
- Full animation pipeline requires Phase 2 delivery.
- The choice of empty vs. armature for v1 is intentional ambiguity (see Unresolved Decisions below).

**Status:** **Accepted** — aligns with phased plan in documentation/PLAN.md.

---

## Unresolved Decisions

### RTMPose-m vs. RTMO for v1
RTMPose-m has higher COCO AP (75.8); RTMO is faster for multi-person. The source plans do not resolve this. Recommendation: try both during M1 benchmarking (backlog item 1.2).

### Blender version target
No Blender version is specified in any source plan. Add-on API compatibility (e.g., `bpy.types.Panel` changes between 3.x and 4.x) is a decision that must be made.

### Hardware requirements
No GPU/CPU requirements are defined. GPU inference needs CUDA-capable hardware; CPU-only targets need RTMPose quantization strategy.

### Distribution model
Open-source marketplace add-on vs. paid release is undefined. No source plan addresses this.

### SMPL licensing path
WHAM requires SMPL/SMPLify registration. It is unclear whether a legal/compliance path exists. If blocked, WHAM should be replaced with an alternative (e.g., VideoPose3D).

# Project Brief — Blender Motion Tracking Enhancement

---

## Purpose

Integrate state-of-the-art human pose tracking into Blender's Video Editor for automatic camera rigging, motion retargeting, and animation. The system takes video input, produces 2D pose tracks with persistent IDs, maps them to Blender empties or armature bones, and optionally lifts to 3D.

## Planning Sources

The project scope is defined by three planning documents:

- **`.pm/PLAN_SUMMARY.md`** — Technical planning summary derived from the master plan and deep research report.
- **`documentation/PLAN.md`** — 18-week phased implementation plan with milestones and phases.
- **`deep-research-report.md`** — Comparative analysis of candidate tracking backends (MMPose, SAM 2, ByteTrack, LoRATv2, WHAM).

---

## Recommended Architecture

```
Video / Still Images
    → Blender Add-on Panel (launch MMPose worker, configure options)
        → MMPose Worker (external Python subprocess, RTMPose inference)
            → 2D Keypoints + Track IDs (cached JSON)
                → Temporal Smoothing + Gap Fill
                    → Blender Empties / Armature Bones
                        → Optional 3D Pose Lift (WHAM, phase-dependent)
                            → Animation Curves in Scene
```

## Primary Backend: MMPose / RTMPose

MMPose with RTMPose is the recommended v1 backend. It produces 2D keypoints directly mappable to Blender bones and empties, with real-time performance (90+ FPS on CPU, 430+ FPS on GPU) and an Apache-2.0 license.

## Target Phases

1. **MMPose Integration** (Weeks 1–4): Video → MMPose → empties with keypoints + track IDs.
2. **Armature Retargeting** (Weeks 5–8): Skeleton bone mapping, automatic armature generation, animation curves.
3. **Multi-Person + Object Tracking** (Weeks 9–12): SAM 2, ByteTrack, RTMO integration.
4. **3D Pose Lifting** (Weeks 13–15): Optional 2D→3D lift via WHAM.
5. **Optimization & Polish** (Weeks 16–18): Latency optimization, TensorRT, UI polish, documentation.

## Why Heavy ML Inference Runs Outside Blender (v1)

Blender ships its own bundled Python distribution. Embedding PyTorch and CUDA inside Blender's Python environment introduces significant complexity:

- **Dependency conflicts:** Blender's Python has its own version and bundled packages. Adding PyTorch (1200+ MB) and CUDA toolkits risks DLL conflicts.
- **Stability:** A crash in the ML worker would take Blender down with it if embedded. Out-of-process keeps Blender stable.
- **Distribution:** Shipping a combined Blender + PyTorch installer is impractical — PyTorch alone is 1.2+ GB with CUDA dependencies.
- **Flexibility:** A separate worker lets users upgrade PyTorch independently, supports GPU/CPU toggle, and enables headless operation on a remote machine.

The out-of-process design is mandated by all three planning sources.

## Why Blender Consumes Cached Tracking Outputs

Communication between Blender and the MMPose worker uses cached JSON files — not in-memory pipes or embedded libraries — because:

- **Inspection & debugging:** JSON files are human-readable. Users can inspect tracking results, compare frames, and debug ID switches without rerunning inference.
- **Idempotency:** Tracking outputs can be cached and reused. Users can tweak visualization, retargeting, or smoothing without re-tracking video.
- **Decoupling:** The worker and Blender can run independently. The worker can process multiple videos; Blender can import any cached result at any time.
- **Simplicity:** File-based exchange avoids complex IPC protocols, shared memory, or network sockets.

## Key Constraints

1. **Not a Python project** — deliverable is a Blender add-on, not a standalone Python repo.
2. **Monocular 3D ambiguity** — 3D pose lifting is optional; depth recovery from a single camera is inherently ambiguous.
3. **Identity consistency** — crowded scenes require robust MOT (phase M6) to prevent ID swaps.
4. **17-joint limitation** — COCO keypoints don't cover spine/neck/jaw/fingers; interpolation is required for full rigs.
5. **SMPL licensing** — WHAM requires SMPL/SMPLify registration, which is a compliance blocker for Phase 4.

## Scope Boundaries (Out of Scope)

- Writing production code (planning only).
- Creating Blender files (.blend).
- Installing ML libraries or setting up environments.
- 3D character generation, facial expression tracking, hand pose tracking, or live camera capture (future extensions).

## Blockers for Execution

1. **Blender version target** — undefined; add-on API compatibility varies across 3.x/4.x.
2. **Hardware requirements** — no GPU/CPU specification defined.
3. **Distribution model** — open-source vs. paid release is undecided.
4. **RTMPose-m vs. RTMO** — not resolved for v1 primary model selection.
5. **SMPL licensing path** — WHAM integration depends on legal/compliance clearance.
